claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder.
Approximately 1050 °C is an optimized SPS temperature for AlCrFeNiSi powder.
AlCrFeNiSi can be consolidated by SPS under moderate pressure in less than 10 minutes and then immediately water-quenched.
SPS followed by rapid quenching will produce a nearly single-phase AlCrFeNiSi alloy.
SPS followed by rapid quenching will produce a compositionally homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi alloy with minimized elemental segregation.
SPS followed by rapid quenching will refine the grain structure of AlCrFeNiSi.
The resulting fine single-phase microstructure will be metastable.
SPS followed by rapid quenching will lower residual stress relative to conventional bulk processing or standard additive manufacturing.
SPS followed by rapid quenching will produce fewer defects than conventional bulk processing or standard additive manufacturing.
Rapid heating and a short hold minimize diffusion during consolidation.
Minimizing diffusion suppresses compositional segregation in the powder-derived alloy.
Immediate quenching arrests phase transformations that would occur during slower cooling.
Immediate quenching locks in a fine, homogeneous microstructure.
The refined and homogeneous microstructure decreases thermal mismatch and thereby limits residual stress and defect development.
The proposed treatment will increase yield strength relative to conventionally bulk-processed or additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed treatment will increase ductility relative to conventionally bulk-processed or additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits significant segregation, high residual stress, and defect formation.
The hypothesis is limited to lab-scale SPS consolidation and may not transfer to other alloy systems or substantially different processing scales.
